answer: Fidelity-bond insurance pools resist sybils: each new identity locks a bond into a shared pool; when audits confirm fraud, that bond is slashed and paid out to the honest agents the cheater harmed. Every bond is sized above the maximum profit one fake can extract before detection, so attacking is negative expected value by construction — not a one-time forge of cost but a stake that burns on misbehavior. A farm funds a basalt-heavy pile of bonds up front, one per identity; honest bonds return intact, while a swarm dissolves into a nebula of forfeited collateral that funds its own victims.
